title: Oscar and the Bakery
premise: Coral Okafor's vineyard survives on one lifeline: a contract with the bakery empire of Oscar Lindqvist, the man she loved and lost twenty years ago. When a snowstorm traps Coral, Oscar, and his business rival Theo in her crumbling estate house, old love and new leverage collide — Oscar must choose between acquiring her vineyard and confessing the sentence he has rehearsed for a decade: that he left to protect her from his family's debts, not because he stopped loving her. As the thaw approaches and Theo's takeover bid tightens, Coral must decide whether safe small steps matter more than the man who taught her to dance. They end by tearing up the contract, marrying in the vineyard's half-restored chapel, and building a bakery-and-wine house together with Theo as an unlikely partner.
about_author: Quentin Villalobos is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, vineyards, and the quiet hours before dawn. He lives in the high desert with his partner and a sourdough starter older than their marriage.

chapters.title: The Contract in the Frost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral prepares to sign the renewal of the bakery contract that keeps her debt-ridden vineyard alive, dreading meeting Oscar Lindqvist for the first time in twenty years. When he arrives early — and a blizzard seals the mountain pass with his rival Theo stranded behind him — she realizes she's trapped with both men. Emotional beat: dread curdling into vertigo as the past walks through her door.

chapters.title: Three at the Table
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral and Oscar POV. Snowbound in the estate house, the three share wine, old photographs, and barbed negotiations. Theo probes the contract's weak points while Oscar and Coral's banter rekindles dangerous intimacy; a power cut forces them to cook together, and Oscar nearly says the rehearsed sentence. Emotional beat: warmth and guilt rising together as duty and desire start to blur.

chapters.title: What He Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Theo presents Coral a buyout that would erase her debts but evict her; Oscar, cornered, confesses the truth — he left twenty years ago because his family's collapse would have ruined her, and he built the bakery empire hoping to buy her freedom back. Coral, furious and undone, rejects both men's rescue. Emotional beat: the climax, where love finally names itself and is refused.

chapters.title: Bread and Vines
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. As the snow melts, Coral counters with her own plan — a partnership, not a purchase — and Oscar signs away the acquisition, choosing her over the empire's expansion. Theo, outmaneuvered and oddly charmed, proposes joining them instead. In spring they marry in the half-restored chapel; the first loaf baked in the new vineyard bakery is shared with the whole valley. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen freely at last.
